paragraphs.source_en: Beside Yoshimoto sat his teacher and military adviser, the eminent Rinzai Zen priest Taigen Sessai, with the faintest trace of a smile upon his face. The senior retainers were arrayed in ranks on either side, a scene utterly unlike the household manner of Oda Nobuhide of Owari.

paragraphs.source_en: Yoshimoto's mother was the daughter of the Middle Counselor Nakamikado, and thus of noble birth. His face was lightly powdered, his brows drawn and his lips colored. His features and attire alike exuded aristocratic elegance, yet his physique and gaze possessed an uncommon virility. In the spring of his eighteenth year, Yoshimoto had succeeded his elder brother as head of the clan; tempered amid turmoil, he had grown into a hardy and formidable warrior.

paragraphs.source_en: If Oda Nobuhide of Owari sought to establish righteous rule by force of arms, Imagawa Yoshimoto aspired to transform the realm through benevolence and virtue. This war was the first stroke dealt by that benevolent man against Owari's champion of martial might.

units.source_en: If Oda Nobuhide of Owari sought to establish righteous rule by force of arms, Imagawa Yoshimoto aspired to transform the realm through benevolence and virtue.

paragraphs.source_en: The first autumn winds should already have been stirring in the mountains, but Suruga was different this year, and the weather remained fiercely hot.

paragraphs.source_en: Neither man regarded Oda Nobuhide as a true enemy. It was merely that Hirotada of Okazaki was too weak; if they stood by, the Oda might use Anshō Castle as a springboard, seize Okazaki in a single stroke, and make matters troublesome. So long as Yoshimoto still intended to enter and rule from the capital, they could not allow a retainer of the Shiba clan to expand his power unchecked.

paragraphs.source_en: In July of the previous year, Yoshimoto's uncle, Hōjō Ujitsuna of Odawara, had died at fifty-five, and his son Ujiyasu had only just succeeded to his great inheritance. Meanwhile, among the Takeda of Kai, father and son Nobutora and Shingen were at odds and quarreled without end. This autumn was the finest opportunity for the Imagawa to attack the Oda, for Yoshimoto had nothing to fear at his rear. Otherwise, Yoshimoto would never have taken the field in person merely to chastise the likes of Oda Nobuhide.

paragraphs.source_en: Throughout his journey from Sunpu toward Okazaki Castle, Imagawa Yoshimoto received an unbroken stream of reports concerning the armies to the east and west. Oda Nobuhide had departed from Nagoya, but no one knew where he had made camp. One thing, however, was certain: he would suddenly appear at Anshō Castle, whose fate was inseparable from Okazaki's, and meet the Imagawa in battle.

paragraphs.source_en: “The Oda are terrifying. Their armies always appear and vanish like phantoms.” The Imagawa army, by contrast, always conducted itself openly and honorably. paragraphs.source_en: They agreed to keep their main force in Okazaki and wait until the Imagawa had defeated the enemy and pursued them as far as the Yahagi River before sallying from the castle to join the attack. Should the Imagawa be defeated, however, the powerful Ōkubo clan based around Kamiwada and its neighboring villages would strike the victorious, withdrawing Oda from the rear and prevent them from coming within a step of Okazaki Castle. In this way, Okazaki Castle could be preserved.
